correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly computes the K_{p,q} grounded inverse by Schur complementation, derives exact reductions for three edge/leader incidences, strictly dominates four of six placement classes, and reduces the remaining comparison to a quadratic P_{p,q}(t) over a positive denominator. The coefficient sign analysis proves precisely the three imbalance regimes and unique positive threshold, with all quantifiers and tie cases. In the actual standalone verify.py, 2,696 direct exact grounded inverse pair comparisons, 2,610 exact formula/optimizer grid checks and integer boundary tests passed. Finite tests are only supplementary to the universal algebraic proof.

value.rationale: A minimally nonbipartite perturbation of a dense two-community network produces a non-obvious optimum relocation only in three sharply constrained part-size families. The exact threshold, objective, all optimizer placements and multiplicities give a complete reusable benchmark for noise-free leader design. It is not a cosmetic rephrasing of an unweighted biclique theorem: t=0 does not determine the sign transition and growing the chord weight leads to a different optimal community in the exceptional regimes.
